method: Built-in image_gen edits, followed by full-size visual inspection of every replacement
reviewCriteria: Screens and controls share the device front
Laptop screen and keyboard face the same viewing side
Devices have visible support and consistent perspective
No sticky notes on laptop lid backs
No reversed handheld phones or calculators

reviewed.notes: Phone now rests flat and face-up on the table; no person holds or operates its rear side. Plates and notebook rest on the same table plane.
Removed the incorrectly oriented laptop. Phone rests face-up on the desk; headphone cable meets the phone edge. No hands or backside display.
Both laptop screens sit above their own keyboards at coherent hinges. Both phones lie flat face-up; no users look at device backs or hold reversed phones.
Phone is supported by a visible dashboard clamp; empty parked cabin removes hand/driver ambiguities. No floating phone.
Tablet screen faces the viewing side and rests on a visible wooden stand; paper review cards lie on the tabletop. Reversed laptop removed.
Garments, tape and phone share a consistent tabletop; phone is flat and screen-up, with no operator looking at its rear.
Laptop and rear-lid sticky notes removed. Phone rests in a visible tripod clamp; recording display faces camera operator/viewer and shows actors beyond it.
All three phone fronts face up on the same desk plane; no camera lenses on front panels or conflicting rear display.
Incorrectly oriented screen removed; practical room and paper plan provide the mission context without device geometry.
Phone rests face-up on the desk; no reversed laptop or person holding a screen backward. Exercise notebook and band are separate grounded objects.
Calculator rests flat with display above an orderly button grid; no reversed handheld calculator or backside laptop display.
Two phones rest flat with their screens upward. Separate cities are represented by a map; the impossible two-laptop arrangement is removed.
Removed the reversed laptop. Phone lies face-up on the counter beside a separate order notebook and empty order tray; no hands operate the rear of a device.
